protocol.freeze: freeze_latest_accepted: development ends when the Builder exits, uses up its 5 accepted submissions or uses up its 5-hour budget; the last accepted submission is frozen and scored on the held-out cases, and a Builder with no accepted submission scores 0. The task's one-stop runs the held-out cases only after a Builder session that ended by itself or after its last submission: when the budget cuts the Builder off, the run stops before the held-out cases and `agentswe result` adds a `budget_exhausted` block (the accepted submissions, the latest one, and score 0 when none was accepted), and `agentswe freeze <run_id>` then freezes the latest accepted submission and runs the held-out cases against it

Release change (2026-10-09): agentloop/evaluator/lower_agent_launcher.py tolerates a Candidate reply disconnect, next to the existing deadline-kill attribution. When the product exited by itself under a valid transport preflight, the only relay errors are BrokenPipe/ConnectionReset on the reply write (with the incomplete observation that disconnect leaves), the relay observation holds the broker's complete HTTP 200 answer, and the broker ledger shows the case window completed with no failure or pending call, the case stays a Candidate outcome; the tolerated errors are recorded as candidate_reply_disconnect, and the judge-evidence checks (agentloop/evaluator/execution_evidence.py prepare_evidence, evaluator/formal_axes.py) accept a broker observation that is incomplete only through those tolerated exchanges. Anything else stays evaluator_failure, and a deadline kill keeps the deadline-kill attribution. Example: the product aborted its own model call after 30 s; the broker completed it at 34.05 s.

Release change (2026-10-10): Docker 29 removes an exited or stopped --rm container asynchronously: for several seconds `docker inspect` still shows it and `docker rm -f` answers "removal of container ... is already in progress" (exit 1); Docker 24 has removed it by then. agentloop/evaluator/broker.py close(): when the stopped --rm broker's removal outlasts the client's 5 s wait, rm answered "already in progress" and became a cleanup error; it is now recorded as removal_in_progress_at_rm and close waits up to 30 s for the container to be gone before inspect decides container_absent. harbor/formal_one_stop.py remove_owned_container waits the same way. Any other rm refusal is judged as before, and a container still present after the wait is not absent. Seen with Docker 29.2.1.
